name: Geometry reader
first: A view that takes all the space proposed to it, and gives its content that size, so that the content can use the numbers.

dependsOn.why: A geometry reader takes part in the steps of layout, and passes its chosen size on to its content.
dependsOn.whyInExample: Line 11 proposes 300 by 200 to the reader, as the renderers propose 300 by 200 on the page of Layout process.

dependsOn.why: The content of a geometry reader is a closure, which SwiftUI calls with the reader's size.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The braces after `GeometryReader` hold a closure whose parameter is `proxy`.

what.is: A geometry reader is a view whose content is a closure. SwiftUI calls the closure with a geometry proxy, a value that holds the reader's own size, so the content can use that size. Apple's documentation says that the reader returns a flexible size to its parent: it takes all the space it is proposed.
what.afterExample: The reader is proposed 300 by 200 points, takes all of it, and gives its content that size through `proxy`.
what.problem: Sometimes a view must know its size in numbers, such as a bar whose width is a share of the space, or a drawing that scales to fit. Layout gives sizes to views, not to code. A geometry reader gives its size to the code of its content.
what.how: In the steps of layout, the reader chooses the whole size it is proposed. It then calls its closure with a proxy that holds that size, and lays out the views that the closure returns inside it.

when.text: Use it when a view's content must be sized as a share of the space, such as a bar that is 40 percent as wide as its container.
Don't use it only to read the size of a view that should choose its own. The reader takes all the space it is proposed, so a reader in a stack can take the space of the views beside it.

parts.name: The proxy, line 3
parts.text: The closure's parameter, `proxy`, is a geometry proxy: a value that SwiftUI makes for the reader, which holds its size. `proxy.size` is the size that the reader chose, as a width and a height.

steps.text: Line 3 makes a geometry reader whose content is a blue `Color` with an `onAppear`, and stores it in `reader`. The closure has not run yet.
Line 10 makes a renderer for `reader`, and line 11 proposes 300 by 200, the size on line 9.
Line 12 asks for the image. The reader takes all of the proposal, and calls its closure with a proxy that holds 300 by 200.
The color appears, and line 6 prints the size that the proxy holds: {{proposed (300.0, 200.0)}}.
The image has the size that the reader chose, and line 13 prints {{300 200}}.

end.text: The reader took the whole proposal, 300 by 200, and gave that size to its content through `proxy`.
